title: MCP Prompt Templates & Dynamic Prompts
description: Design reusable MCP prompt templates with dynamic variable injection and context-aware template selection.

data.text: Prompt Templates as First-Class MCP Resources

MCP prompt templates allow servers to expose reusable, parameterized prompt definitions that clients can invoke. Unlike static prompts, template-based prompts support dynamic variable injection — the client provides values at invocation time, and the server renders the final prompt. This enables context-aware prompts that adapt to user role, document type, or conversation history.

The MCP specification defines prompt templates through the Prompts capability. A server advertises available templates via ListPROMPTS, each with a name, description, and arguments schema. Clients invoke a template via CreatePROMPT, passing argument values. The server returns a rendered prompt with messages ready for LLM consumption.

data.text: Dynamic prompt templates select different message sequences based on runtime context. For example, a code review template might include security-focused instructions for production code but a lighter touch for prototype code. The template engine evaluates conditions at invocation time and renders the appropriate prompt.

data.text: Version-control your prompt templates alongside code. Use semantic versioning for templates that affect LLM behavior. Breaking changes to prompts should trigger tests that validate expected outputs, just like code changes.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: MCP prompt templates expose parameterized, reusable prompts via the Prompts capability
Dynamic variable injection allows context-aware prompts that adapt at invocation time
Conditional template engines enable different prompt variants per context
Version-control prompt templates and test breaking changes like code
Templates can include conversation history, tool specifications, and role context
data.takeaway: MCP prompt templates turn ad-hoc prompts into reusable, parameterized, and version-controlled assets that scale across teams and use cases.
